a11yFix_missing-label: Set contentDescription (Android) or accessibilityLabel (iOS) to the action, e.g. “Close”.
a11yFix_touch-target: Grow the tappable area with padding or minHeight/minWidth; the icon itself can stay small.
a11yFix_duplicate-label: Make each label say what it acts on: “Delete card *1234” instead of “Delete”.
a11yFix_low-contrast: Darken the text or lighten the background until the ratio reaches the requirement.
a11yFix_input-without-label: Give the field a visible label linked to it (labelFor / accessibilityLabel).
a11yFix_redundant-role: Remove “button”, “icon”, “image” from the label: the platform announces the role.
a11yFix_not-accessible: Set isAccessibilityElement = true on the control or its container.
a11yFix_non-text-contrast: Use a darker icon or outline, at least 3 : 1 against what is behind it.
a11yFix_target-spacing: Enlarge the targets or add space between them.
a11yFix_nested-clickable: Make either the row or the inner control clickable, or give the inner one a custom action.
a11yFix_hidden-focusable: Hide the element from accessibility while it is invisible (accessibilityElementsHidden / isAccessibilityElement = false).
a11yFix_non-descriptive-label: Write the label as a person would say it: “Share”, not “shareButton”.
a11yFix_hint-only-input: Add a persistent label above the field and keep the hint for an example value.
a11yFix_state-missing: Use a real Switch/CheckBox or expose the state (stateDescription / accessibilityValue).
a11yFix_text-clipping: Let the text wrap to more lines, or shorten it; check again with the largest font.
a11yFix_reading-order: Order the views in the layout as they appear, or set accessibilityTraversalBefore/After.

finding_android-allow-backup_why: With allowBackup on, tokens and databases of the app can be copied off the phone with adb backup or a cloud backup.
finding_android-allow-backup_fix: Set android:allowBackup="false", or limit what is backed up with dataExtractionRules / fullBackupContent.
finding_android-debuggable_why: Anyone with the phone can attach a debugger and read the app's memory and files. Fine for a test build, never for a release.
finding_android-debuggable_fix: Make sure the release build type has debuggable false.
finding_android-cleartext_why: usesCleartextTraffic lets the app send data without encryption, which anyone on the network can read.
finding_android-cleartext_fix: Remove usesCleartextTraffic="true"; allow HTTP for specific test hosts in network_security_config only.
finding_android-exported_why: An exported component without a permission can be called by any app on the phone, bypassing the app's own screens and checks.
finding_android-exported_fix: Set android:exported="false" where other apps do not need it, or protect it with android:permission.
finding_android-dangerous-permissions_wh: {{list}}. Each one needs a reason the store review and the users accept.
finding_android-dangerous-permissions_fi: Remove the permissions the app does not use; check that each one asked at runtime has a clear explanation.
finding_android-target-sdk_why: Google Play refuses updates that target an old Android version, and the app misses newer privacy protections.
finding_android-target-sdk_fix: Raise targetSdkVersion to {{min}} or newer and retest permissions and background work.
finding_android-test-only_title: The APK is marked test only
finding_android-test-only_why: android:testOnly builds install only with adb install -t and cannot go to the store. Usually a build from the IDE's Run button.
finding_android-test-only_fix: Take the build from the CI pipeline instead of the IDE.
finding_ios-ats-arbitrary-loads_why: NSAllowsArbitraryLoads lets the app use plain HTTP and weak TLS everywhere. App Review asks why.
finding_ios-ats-arbitrary-loads_fix: Remove NSAllowsArbitraryLoads; list only the hosts that really need an exception under NSExceptionDomains.
finding_ios-ats-insecure-domain_why: Traffic to these hosts can travel without encryption: {{domain}}.
finding_ios-ats-insecure-domain_fix: Move the hosts to HTTPS and drop NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads.
finding_ios-get-task-allow_why: get-task-allow lets a debugger attach to the app. Development builds have it; App Store and TestFlight builds must not.
finding_ios-get-task-allow_fix: Sign the build for testers with an ad hoc or distribution profile.
finding_ios-file-sharing_title: App files are open in Finder and Files
finding_ios-file-sharing_why: UIFileSharingEnabled shows the app's Documents folder to anyone with the phone and a cable.
finding_ios-file-sharing_fix: Turn file sharing off, or keep sensitive data out of Documents.
finding_ios-url-schemes_why: Any app or web page can open these links. Check that each handler validates its input and asks before acting.
finding_ios-url-schemes_fix: Test every deep link with unexpected and missing parameters; prefer universal links for sensitive actions.
finding_ios-profile-expiring_title: The provisioning profile expires in {{days}} days
finding_ios-profile-expiring_why: When it expires the app stops launching on test devices.
finding_ios-profile-expiring_fix: Renew the profile and rebuild before it runs out.

finding_log-crash_why: An uncaught exception closed the app in front of the user.
finding_log-crash_fix: Open the line for the stack trace and attach it to the bug with the steps that led there.
finding_log-native-crash_why: Native code (C/C++, a library or the WebView) crashed the process.
finding_log-native-crash_fix: Attach the tombstone (adb bugreport) and the steps; the developers need the native stack.
finding_log-anr_why: {{reason}}. The system offered to close the app: the main thread was busy for too long.
finding_log-anr_fix: Note what was on screen and what you tapped; attach the log and /data/anr traces.
finding_log-strict-mode_why: Disk or network work on the main thread makes the interface stutter and can lead to ANRs.
finding_log-strict-mode_fix: Report the screen where it happens; the developers move the work off the main thread.
finding_log-ios-exception_why: An uncaught Objective-C or Swift exception closed the app.
finding_log-ios-exception_fix: Attach the crash report from the device (Settings › Privacy › Analytics) and the steps.

finding_traffic-error_why: The server answered with an error. Check whether the app shows the user something sensible.
finding_traffic-error_fix: Attach the request and the response to the bug; if the error is expected, add it to the expected errors.
finding_traffic-slow_why: {{ms}} ms with a limit of {{limit}} ms. The user waits with a spinner.
finding_traffic-slow_fix: Report it with the timings; if the endpoint is slow by nature, give it its own limit.
finding_traffic-duplicate_why: The same request went {{count}} times within {{windowMs}} ms: extra load and battery, sometimes double actions.
finding_traffic-duplicate_fix: Report the screen it happens on; polling and allowed repeats can be described in the expected repeats.

wsAppsError_notPaired: The iPhone is not paired with this Mac: unlock it and tap Trust.
wsAppsError_failed: Could not read the apps on the device.
quickSigningNoTeam: A real iPhone needs WebDriverAgent signed, and this Mac has no development certificate. Add an Apple ID in Xcode → Settings → Accounts and create an Apple Development certificate.
quickSigningPickTeam: This Mac has {{count}} development teams. Pick the one to sign WebDriverAgent with.
settingsDevicesText: What sessions on real devices need.
settingsIosPurpose: Appium puts its WebDriverAgent app on a real iPhone, and Xcode has to sign it with a development certificate
settingsIosNoTeam: This Mac has no development certificate
settingsIosNoTeamHow: Xcode → Settings → Accounts → “+” → Apple ID (work or personal). Then Manage Certificates → “+” → Apple Development. Then press “Look again”.
settingsIosPick: There are several teams: pick the one your iPhone is registered with.
settingsIosBundleIdHint: Empty: the team’s own ID. Change it if your team already has a profile for WebDriverAgent.
settingsIosPhoneSteps: On the iPhone: turn on Developer Mode (Settings → Privacy & Security), unlock it and trust this Mac. With a personal team, after the first start allow the developer in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.
sessionHintWdaTitle: WebDriverAgent did not start on the iPhone
sessionHintWdaText: Xcode could not build or sign WebDriverAgent. Check the development team in Settings → Devices, that your Xcode supports the phone’s iOS version, and that the iPhone has Developer Mode on, is unlocked and trusts this Mac. The first build takes a few minutes.
sessionHintNoActivityTitle: The app does not start on the device
sessionHintNoActivityText: The device does not have this app, or it cannot be opened from the launcher. Pick an app installed on this device at the top.
aiDailyLimitHint: Nothing more is sent in a day, so the quota is not used up.
aiConsentSwitchHint: Without it the AI check sends nothing and asks you first.
logsScopeNoAppHint: Pick an app at the top to see only its lines
logsSearchError: The regular expression has an error: {{error}}
logsAppNone: No app picked: the whole device is shown
buildsPipelinePlaceholder: A GitLab pipeline or job link (or just ⌘V on this page)
buildsPipelineBadLink: This is not a GitLab pipeline or job link
buildsPipelineWaiting: Waiting for {{job}}: {{status}}. Asking GitLab every 10 s.
buildsPipelineManual: Job {{job}} waits to be started by hand
buildsPipelineChooseBuild: The archive has several builds. Pick one; next time the same kind is taken:
buildsPipelineNoJobs: The pipeline has none of the jobs to take the build from. Change the jobs below.
buildsPipelineNoArtifacts: Job {{job}} finished without a build in its artifacts
buildsPipelineRetry: GitLab did not answer: {{error}}. Trying again.
buildsPipelineAuto: Install as soon as it is ready
buildsPipelineError_notSetUp: GitLab is not set up yet: add the site and a token in Settings
buildsPipelineError_otherSite: The link is to another GitLab than the one set up: change the site in Settings
buildsPipelineError_notFound: The pipeline is not there, or the token cannot see it
settingsBuildsText: Where the build comes from when you paste a GitLab pipeline link. Written once per project.
buildSourcesPurpose: For each project: the jobs to wait for and the file to take, apart for simulators and real devices
buildSourcesEmpty: No rules yet. Add one here, or just paste a pipeline link in Builds.
buildRuleProjectHint: The project’s path in GitLab, its end (android/ap24v6), or a pattern with * (p24-front-end-mob/*)
buildRuleJobs: Jobs to wait for the build
buildRuleJobsSame: Empty: the same as for the simulator
buildRuleJobsHint: Jobs in order of preference: the first that finished with a build is taken; while one runs, Station#1 waits. The file is a pattern with * for an archive with several builds.
buildsPipelineNoRule: {{project}} has no rule yet. Say once where its build comes from:
buildsPipelineMissing: The jobs are not in the pipeline yet, waiting
buildsPipelinePickDevices: Pick devices: the build for a simulator and for a real device may differ
proxyDupExpectedHint: poll <ms> — polling: a series of requests is fine, a duplicate only when sooner than the interval. allow <N> in <time> — up to N times within a time (30s, 2m). ignore — never a duplicate. The first matching line applies.
proxyContractRequired: What requests and responses must have (one rule per line)
proxyContractHint: header:<Name> — a request header, response.header:<Name> — a response header, response.body:<path.to.field> — a field in the JSON of a successful response. Several per line are fine.
proxyWhy_slowRule: Took {{duration}} with the limit {{limit}} from the rule “{{rule}}”.
finding_traffic-contract_why: Required parts are missing: {{missing}}. The backend or the app breaks the agreement.
finding_traffic-contract_fix: Report the screen it happens on with the request and the response; if the rule is outdated, fix it in the traffic rules.
settingsProfilesText: Each project has its own proxy and log rules, filters, accessibility, build sources and Jira bug fields. The tools work by the profile picked in the title bar.
settingsProfileDeleteHint: A backup is saved first; the profile can be brought back from it.
settingsProfileLast: The last profile cannot be deleted
settingsProfileAppsHint: The station works with the app for the platform of the active device. Install a build of another project’s app and the station switches to that profile.
settingsSourceHint: The agent reads the code from these copies. A copy belongs to the station: switching a branch discards its local changes, so use a separate clone rather than a developer’s working copy.
settingsSourceEmpty: No repository yet. Add a local copy so the agent can see the app code.
settingsSourceNoFolder: No folder on this Mac yet.
settingsSourceRemoveAsk: Remove {{name}} from the profile? The folder stays on disk.
settingsSourceWarn_detached: The repository is not on a branch (detached HEAD). Switch to a branch.
settingsSourceWarn_notDev: The branch is {{branch}}, not the development branch. The agent sees this one.
settingsSourceWarn_changes: Uncommitted changes: {{count}}. Switching a branch discards them.
settingsSourceWarn_noBranch: There is no {{branch}} branch in the repository.
settingsSourceSubmoduleOff: not checked out, the agent does not see it
settingsSourceSwitchClean: No local changes, nothing to discard.
settingsSourceSwitchDiscard: To be discarded ({{count}}): changed files are restored, new ones are deleted. This cannot be undone.
settingsSourceErr_missing: The folder is gone. Choose it again.
settingsSourceErr_notRepo: This is not a git repository. Choose a folder with a copy of the repository.
settingsSourceErr_gitMissing: Git not found. Install the developer tools: xcode-select --install.
settingsSourceErr_noFolder: No folder on this Mac yet. Choose one.
settingsSourceErr_fetch: Could not fetch from origin. Check the network and access to the repository.
settingsSourceErr_timeout: Git did not answer in time. Try again.
settingsSourceErr_pull: Could not pull: the branch has diverged from origin or there is no access. The station only pulls fast-forward.
settingsSourceErr_discard: Could not discard local changes; the branch was not switched.
settingsSourceErr_noBranch: No such branch locally or in origin. Fetch from origin and try again.
settingsSourceErr_submodules: The branch is switched, but the submodules did not update.
settingsSourceErr_noPrevious: There is no branch to go back to.
settingsProfileAppsUnplaced: Not placed yet: {{ids}}. Type them into the Android or iOS field.
settingsTransferPurpose: Move to another Mac, share with the team, go back to earlier ones
settingsExportWhat: What to put in the file:
settingsNoSecrets: Tokens and keys are not exported: on another Mac they are entered again.
settingsImportBackupNote: A copy of the current settings is saved before the import.
settingsImportError_json: The file is broken: it is not JSON. {{detail}}
settingsImportError_format: This is not a station settings file. Pick a file saved with “Export”.
settingsImportError_version: The file was made by a newer station (format {{detail}}). Update the station and try again.
settingsImportError_shape: The file has wrong values in “{{detail}}”. Nothing was changed; export the file again.
settingsImportTokens: Tokens do not travel. This Mac has none yet for: {{list}}. Enter them in “Integrations”.
settingsRestoreAsk: Put the settings back to this copy?
settingsRestoreHint: Profiles and station settings become as in the copy. The current ones are saved as a copy of their own.
wsProjectNoApps: This project has no app yet. Add the Android package and the iOS bundle id in “Manage”, and the station takes the one for the active device.
deskCheckServerOn: The Appium server is running and ready for a session.
deskCheckProxyOn: The proxy is listening and recording the device's traffic.
deskCheckProxyOff: The proxy starts as soon as you open the Proxy tab.
deskCheckLogsOn: The device log is recording; the rules look for crashes and ANRs.
deskCheckLogsOff: The log starts recording as soon as you open the Logs tab.
deskCheck_jiraOn: Jira is connected: bugs are filed with a duplicate check.
deskCheck_jiraOff: Jira is not connected: bugs cannot be filed without it.
deskCheck_gitlabOn: GitLab is connected: builds come from the pipelines.
deskCheck_gitlabOff: GitLab is not connected: builds have to be dropped in by hand.
deskDeviceActiveOk: The device is connected and picked for every tool.
deskDeviceStartable: Off: start it and it becomes active.
deskNoSessionLine: Problems show up here once the proxy, the log or a screen audit runs.
deskFix_node: install Node.js 22 LTS with nvm and restart the terminal.
deskFix_shellEnv: run the command in a terminal and see where the profile stops or what it asks; remove the prompt or wrap it in a [[ -t 0 ]] check.
deskFix_appium: update Appium to a stable version.
deskFix_appiumMissing: install Appium with the button or the command.
deskFix_driver: install the driver with the button or the command.
deskFix_androidSdk: install Android Studio: it brings the SDK.
deskFix_androidSdkMissing: point ANDROID_HOME at the real SDK folder and restart the terminal.
deskFix_androidHome: add ANDROID_HOME to your shell profile and restart the terminal.
deskFix_adb: install platform-tools with the SDK Manager.
deskFix_javaHome: set JAVA_HOME in your shell profile and restart the terminal.
deskFix_xcode: install Xcode from the App Store and select it as the developer tools.
deskFix_server: start our own Appium with one click.
deskFix_device_xcodeTooOld: update Xcode from the App Store to a version that supports this iOS, then select it with the command.
deskFix_deviceBroken: download the system image in Android Studio → Device Manager, or delete this emulator.
deskFix_deviceUnauthorized: unlock the phone and allow USB debugging for this computer.
deskFix_deviceOffline: restart adb, then plug the cable in again.
deskFix_deviceDisconnected: connect the device by cable or on the same network.
deskNoActiveDevice: No active device: pick one below.
deskNewTestLead: What was collected is cleared so new problems do not mix with the old ones. Rules, settings, the device and the Appium session stay.
deskResetBuildSub: {{version}} · usually kept for the next test
journalNoPrevious: There is no journal of the previous run
agentEmpty: Ask about the screen, a request, the log or the task. The agent sees what is picked and takes the rest from the station itself.
agentPlaceholder: Message to the agent (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line)
agentDeepHint: A larger read budget for this turn: for impact analysis and hard questions. Costs more, digs deeper.
agentUndoConflictTitle: This was changed again after the agent
agentUndoConflict: Rolling back restores the value from before the agent and wipes the change made by hand.
agentPermissionDiscard: To be discarded ({{count}}), cannot be undone:
agentBudget: The agent has read {{count}} characters of station data this turn and wants more.
agentReadMoreMessage: You may read more station data, the budget is extended.
agentConsentTitle: Send the project’s data to the agent?
agentConsentText: The agent runs in the Kiro cloud (AWS) under your account’s rules. For this profile it gets what it takes itself:
agentConsent_task: the task, linked tasks and Confluence pages
agentConsent_code: the app code from the given repositories
agentConsent_screens: the screen tree, a screenshot only when asked
agentConsentNever: Authorization headers, cookies, tokens and keys never go; card numbers, phones and emails are masked.
agentCreditLimit: {{spent}} cr. spent today, over your daily threshold. Continue?
agentError_missing: Kiro CLI not found. Install it and check the environment on the desk.
agentError_login: Kiro is not signed in. Run kiro-cli login in a terminal.
agentError_credits: Kiro credits ran out or a limit was hit. See the plan in the agent settings.
agentError_network: No connection to Kiro. Check the network.
agentError_stopped: Kiro stopped. The next message starts it again.
agentPlanUnknown: The Kiro plan shows up after the first conversation with the agent.
agentBudgetHint: Every character the agent reads from the station stays in the conversation and is paid for on every later turn.
agentConsentGiven: This profile’s data may go to the agent.
agentConsentNotYet: The station asks before the first message in this profile.
agentInstructionsProject: Project instructions (go with the profile export)
agentInstructionsProjectHint: About the app: what it is, test accounts (no passwords), glossary, what to watch for.
agentInstructionsPersonalHint: How to answer you: language, style, report format.
agentInstructionsHint: The agent gets them in this order. Changes apply from the next conversation.
agentMcpHint: Each server’s tool descriptions take context on every turn: switch off the servers you do not need now.
agentMcpError_auth: The server refused: wrong token or no access.
agentMcpError_command: Command not found. Check that it is installed.
agentMcpError_unreachable: The server does not answer at this address.
agentMcpError_incomplete: Give the server’s address or command.
agentMcpError_other: The server answered with an error.
settingsAgentText: The agent on Kiro CLI sees the station’s data, the code and the task, and sets the station up with your permission. Here are its credits, instructions and MCP servers.
settingsGroup_agentStation: Agent: station instructions, MCP and budgets
doctorCheck_kiro_ok: Kiro CLI {{version}}: V3 engine present, signed in
doctorCheck_kiroMissing_warn: Kiro CLI not found: the station agent needs it
doctorCheck_kiroV3_warn: Kiro CLI {{version}} has no V3 engine: the agent needs V3
deskFix_kiroMissing: Install Kiro CLI with the command below and check again.
deskFix_kiroLogin: Sign in to Kiro in a terminal.
taskNone: No task chosen: give a Jira key or link and the station gathers its context.
taskPlaceholder: PAY-123 or a link to the task
taskAsk: Ask the agent about the task
taskAskPrompt: Tell me briefly about task {{key}}: what changes and what matters to check.
taskImpactPrompt: Make the impact analysis of task {{key}} by the method in the station instructions and hand the checklist over with impact_report.
taskSection_commits: Commits with the key in the development branch: {{count}}
taskNoMrs: No merge request links in the comments of the task or its linked tasks.
taskError_badKey: No task key there. Give a key (PAY-123) or a link to a Jira task.
taskError_jiraNotSetUp: Jira is not connected, so the task context cannot be gathered.
taskError_notFound: No such task, or the token cannot see it.
taskError_access: No access to the task: check the Jira token.
taskError_failed: Could not gather the task context.
taskImpactStale: stale: new commits or task changes
taskImpactRemoved: Items gone since the last analysis: {{count}}
taskNoiseWhy: Why is it noise? The agent will take it into account next time.
memoryTextPlaceholder: One fact or one rule, up to 300 characters
memorySimilar: A similar note is already there: “{{text}}”
memoryError_secret: Looks like a secret (token, password, key). Remove it and save again.
memoryError_personal: There is personal data here (card number, phone, email). Remove it.
memoryError_noTask: No task is chosen: pick another scope.
memoryWhyUndone: Rolled back: {{change}}. Why? I will keep it as a correction — or skip it.
memorySummarizePrompt: Look through our conversation about task {{key}} and propose up to 5 memory notes with memory_propose: corrections, lessons about the app. Only what later tasks will need.
memoryPinnedBudget: Pinned notes go into every conversation: {{used}} / {{budget}} characters
memoryEmpty: No notes yet. They appear when you correct the agent or press “Remember”.
memoryPruneAsk: Delete {{count}} notes not used for {{days}} days?
memoryHint: The agent saves and changes nothing itself: it only proposes. Project notes go with the profile export, personal ones never.
goalsProposePrompt: Propose session goals for task {{key}}: from the impact analysis (make it if there is none) take everything the station can count by itself and hand it over with goal_propose.
goalsEmpty: No goals yet. The agent proposes them from the task and the code, or add your own — the station counts them by itself, without AI.
goalAsk: Ask the agent whether it is a bug
goalAskPrompt: Goal “{{title}}” failed: {{evidence}} {{note}}. Find out whether it is a bug and say why, briefly.
goalType_field: a field in a request or response
goalExpectOn: The screen to expect it on (optional)
goalProblem_value: Give a value (a valid regex for a pattern).
goalReportSent: Report added as a comment on {{key}}
goalReportFailed: Could not send the report to Jira.
stationPageText: Whether this Mac is ready to test and which devices it sees.
taskEmptyTitle: Which task are you working on?
taskEmptyText: The station gathers the task, linked tasks, Confluence pages and MRs, and the agent makes the impact analysis.
taskGitlabOff: GitLab is not connected: MRs are shown as links, without changes and files.
